VZ.rationale: Verizon presents a mildly attractive fundamental picture with improving trajectory. Q1 2026 showed solid execution: revenue grew 2.9% YoY to $34.44B, EPS rose 4.3% to $1.20, and the company delivered its first positive Q1 postpaid phone net adds in 13 years (55K). Adjusted EBITDA margin hit a record 38.9%, and free cash flow grew 4% YoY to ~$3.8B. Management raised EPS guidance to 5-6% growth and expects postpaid net adds in the upper half of 750K-1M range. The Frontier acquisition expands fiber passings to ~30M, creating a long-term broadband growth lever. However, wireless service revenue declined ~1% YoY in Q1 due to temporary headwinds (outage credits, promotional amortization), and the company carries ~$120B in debt with leverage at ~2.6x, above its 2.0-2.25x target. Valuation is attractive: at $48.27, the P/E of 11.4x is near the low end of its 11-21x 12-month range and well below the ~17-18x where it traded for most of 2025, suggesting the market has not fully priced in the improving fundamentals. The 6%+ dividend yield and 20 consecutive years of increases provide income support. Rising 10-year Treasury yields (4.57%) create a mild headwind for yield-oriented equities, and competitive pressure from T-Mobile remains a structural risk. No clear near-term dated catalyst beyond the Q2 earnings expected ~July 21, 2026.
